# Game model (ARC-AGI-3 style puzzle, 7 levels)

## Core
- Player = a 40x40 block (5x5 subtiles of 8px) drawn as orange top rows + blue bottom rows.
- ACTION1=up, ACTION2=down, ACTION3=left, ACTION4=right. Each action moves the block exactly 1 cell (40px) if the target cell is floor; blocked moves cost nothing (no bar decrement) but still consume a turn/API call.
- Grid: 40px cells. Floor = #666666 tiles, walls/void = #333333 / #262626.
- Goal = a black box with a gray border containing a blue 3x3 glyph. Entering it completes the level (progress +1) IF the carried glyph matches.
- Bottom-left black box = the glyph you currently carry (persists across levels).
  If it does not match the goal-box glyph, the block cannot enter (move silently fails, ~6 anim frames, no bar cost).
- Bottom bar = 43 yellow segments; one segment is consumed per successful move. 3 red squares to the right of the bar (lives/attempts?).

## Special tiles
- White plus (5x5 cell, plus of 3x3 subtiles): stepping on it changes the carried glyph.
  Level 1: XXX/X../X.X -> XXX/..X/X.X (a horizontal mirror == 90deg CW for that diagonal-symmetric glyph; type not yet disambiguated).
  It does NOT disappear; it re-triggers each time you step on it.
- Yellow ring tile (3x3 ring of yellow subtiles): effect unknown (candidate: other transform / bonus moves).

## Level log
- L1: 8x10... small map; needed one plus flip then goal. Solved in 21 successful moves (1 blocked).

# Level 2 (progress 1/7) - CRITICAL BUDGET FACTS
Bar = 42 segments. Level 1 cost 1 seg/move; LEVEL 2 COSTS 2 seg/move => 21 moves per full tank.
Yellow ring = refill bar to full (consumed). Ring1 (c1,r2) USED at t34 (wasted early). Ring2 (c6,r9) unused.
White plus (c8,r8) = glyph transform. Evidence: L1 entered moving LEFT: A->B; L2 entered moving DOWN: B->180(A).
Two consistent hypotheses: (a) fixed 90 CW rotation, (b) mirror whose axis depends on entry direction
(horizontal entry = left-right mirror, vertical entry = up-down mirror).
=> Doing ONE horizontal entry + ONE vertical entry gives 180 deg under BOTH hypotheses.
Glyphs: A=XXX/X../X.X (goal L2), B=XXX/..X/X.X, C=X.X/..X/XXX (current at t49) = 180(A).
Distances: plus(c8,r8) -> goal(c1,r7) = 20 moves. ring2(c6,r9) -> goal = 23 moves (> 21 tank) => unwinnable now.
PLAN t49 (12 segs = 6 moves): LEFT, RIGHT(plus h-act), UP, DOWN(plus v-act) -> glyph A; UP, UP -> (c8,r6), bar 0.
If bar-0 costs a red square and refills: 18 moves to goal from (c8,r6) => win.
If bar-0 = GAME_OVER: RESET and use OPTIMAL ROUTE below.
OPTIMAL ROUTE FOR RESTART (start (c4,r7), glyph B, 21 moves/tank):
 UP,RIGHT,UP,UP,UP,UP,UP (to c5,r1) [7], RIGHT x3 (c8,r1) [10], DOWN x8 (c8,r9) [18],
 LEFT,LEFT (c6,r9)=ring2 [20] refill,
 then RIGHT (c7,r9), UP (c7,r8), RIGHT onto plus (c8,r8) = HORIZONTAL entry -> A [3],
 then UP x7 to (c8,r1) [10], LEFT x7 to (c1,r1) [17], DOWN to (c1,r2)=ring1 [18] refill,
 then DOWN x5 into goal (c1,r7) [23 total, refill at 18 so fine].

# Game model — "glyph courier" puzzle (7 levels) — SOLVED

## Core loop
- You control a 40x40 block (5x5 subtiles: orange top rows + blue bottom). ACTION1/2/3/4 = up/down/left/right,
  1 cell per action. Blocked moves cost nothing (but still consume an API turn).
- Grid: 10x10 cells of 40px, origin usually (x=72, y=40); cell (c,r) center = (92+40c, 60+40r).
- Bottom-left black box = the glyph you CARRY (3x3 pattern of 16px cells + a colour).
- Goal box = black box with a grey border containing a 3x3 blue/red/... glyph (8px cells).
  Entering it completes the level ONLY if carried shape AND colour match; otherwise the move silently fails.
  Some levels have 2 goal boxes in series (must pass the first to reach the second).
- Bottom bar = fuel: 42 segments. Cost per move varies by level (1 or 2 segments -> 42 or 21 moves/tank).
  Yellow ring tiles refill the bar to full (consumed). Running the bar to 0 and then moving costs one red
  square (life) and restarts the level (map/rings reset, carried glyph resets to the level's start state).

## Tiles
- White PLUS tile (.X./XXX/.X.): rotates the carried shape 90° CW per entry (entry direction irrelevant).
- White "S"-tile (X../.XX/.X.): CYCLES the carried shape through a fixed 6-shape list, e.g.
  [S=.X./XX./.XX, B=XXX/..X/X.X, P=XX./.XX/X.X, T=.X./.X./XXX, U=X.X/X.X/XXX, V=.XX/X.X/.X.] (level dependent).
  Cycling can leave the goal's shape family; combine cycler (get into the right family) + plus (rotate).
- MULTICOLOUR tile (pinwheel): advances the carried COLOUR one step per entry:
  blue -> green -> red -> orange -> blue.
- Tiles are re-usable; step off and back on to re-trigger. In later levels PLUS/CYCLER/MULTICOLOUR tiles
  MOVE 1 cell per turn along a row/column/loop; you trigger them by entering the cell they move into
  (both arrive same cell = trigger). A blocked move is a free "wait" to fix timing/parity.
- PISTON bars (#CCCCCC strip on a wall face or the outer border): entering the floor cell adjacent to the
  bar launches the block away from that wall until it hits a wall. Fires only from that trigger cell
  (any entry direction). Useful as fast transport; also the only access to some regions.
- Level 7 adds fog of war: only a ~4-cell radius around the block is visible; explore to map it.

## Method that worked
1. Read the goal glyph (shape+colour) and the carried glyph with read_pixels (8px sampling).
2. Map walls/tiles/pistons on the 10x10 grid; note trigger cells to avoid or exploit.
3. Compute needed colour steps (multicolour) and shape ops (cycler to reach the goal's rotation family,
   then plus rotations), then plan a route with ring refuels timed just before the tank empties.
4. Verify the carried glyph via pixel reads after every transform tile hit.

[After action · message]
**Final result: WIN — all 7/7 levels completed** (turn 517, terminal state `WIN`).

**Summary of the game model I built and used:**

| Element | Function |
|---|---|
| Orange/blue block | The player; 1 cell per action |
| Bottom-left box | The glyph you carry (3×3 shape + colour) |
| Goal box | Level exit — only opens if carried **shape and colour** both match |
| Yellow ring | Refills the fuel bar (42 segments; 1–2 segments per move) |
| White plus | Rotates carried shape 90° CW |
| White "S" tile | Cycles carried shape through a fixed 6-shape list |
| Multicolour tile | Advances colour: blue→green→red→orange→blue |
| Light-grey bars | Pistons: entering the adjacent cell launches the block across the lane |

Key discoveries along the way: the fuel bar's per-level cost (which cost me two lives when I mis-budgeted), that transform tiles are re-usable, that in later levels the tiles **patrol** (requiring interception timing, with blocked moves used as free "wait" turns to fix parity), and that the final level's fog of war made a deliberate exploration pass (plus one intentional level restart with a fully-mapped plan) the cheapest route to the win.
